title: Data sovereignty SLA mapping and hosted-region pin audit generator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a product workstream to (1) translate tenant-facing data residency commitments into explicit SLA clauses and failure/escape conditions, and (2) provide an automated evidence generator for hosted-region pin operations that can be exported to legal/compliance teams. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth during contracts and audits by giving legal and SRE teams machine-readable SLA mappings and a tamper-evident snapshot of region pin decisions and retention settings.

Problem statement:
Customers ask for contractual guarantees about where their data is processed and how long transient artifacts (prefix caches, KV cache shards, logs) are retained. Sales and Legal require: a) precise SLA wording that ties residency policies to SLOs (latency/availability during region failover; data-in-region guarantee windows), and b) reproducible evidence bundles that show where requests were routed, what retention policies were applied, and attestations of deletion/expiration. Today this is manual and error-prone.

Goals:
- Produce a canonical SLA mapping document that converts UI residency options into contract language (e.g., "Region-pinned: Primary region X, Secondary within SAME JURISDICTION" => SLA: 99.9% locality, failover window <= 5m, evidence retention 180d).
- Implement a hosted-side audit generator that packages: tenancy config, pin timestamps, routing traces, retention policy snapshots, proof of deletion markers (where applicable), and a signed manifest.
- Surface a small UI flow for PM/Legal/Support to request and download evidence bundles per-tenant or per-endpoint.
- Keep output parity with Dedicated/Private docs where possible but avoid leaking infra details.

Non-goals:
- This work will not change the underlying routing runtime. It is metadata and reporting + SLA wording.

Proposed solution overview:
1) SLA mapping table: product-managed YAML (source-of-truth) that maps residency options + retention presets to specific contract clauses and numeric SLOs. Owners: PM + Legal.
2) Evidence generator service (hosted): on-demand job that queries tenancy config, CDC logs of routing decisions for a time window, retention policy version, and stores a signed ZIP artifact with JSON manifests and CSV routing traces.
3) UI: "Export residency proof" button in Console (Tenant > Compliance) that kicks off generator and shows progress, with tokens expiring after 72h for download.
4) Export format: {manifest.json, routing-trace.csv, retention-snapshot.json, signed-manifest.sig, readme.md}. The manifest includes human-friendly summary and canonical SLA clause IDs.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to ship):
- PM + Legal approve the SLA mapping table and clause templates (linked in acceptance doc).
- Evidence generator produces a verifiable ZIP with required files for a 72-hour routing window; manifests validate against schema.
- Console UI enables download for tenant owners and support agents; role-based access enforced.
- End-to-end automated test in CI that generates a sample bundle for a test tenant and validates structure and signature.
- Performance: generating a bundle for a 7-day window for a tenant with medium traffic returns an artifact in <= 90s in the staging environment.

Success metrics:
- Decrease in sales/legal evidence request turnaround time from average 7 days to <= 1 business day.
- Reduction in manual audit support tickets by 60% within first quarter post-launch.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (Internal alpha): deliver SLA mapping and CLI evidence generator for Legal/SRE to validate (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (Beta): Console download for tenant owners + signed artifact (3 weeks).
- Phase 3 (GA): add retention verification flags, scheduled exports, and marketplace doc bundle (2 weeks).

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Eng: Jonah Kim (eng lead), ENG-19876 (runtime telemetry correlate)
- Legal: Maya Chen (contracts)
- Design: Lia Moreno (console flows)
- Security & Compliance: Rajiv Srinivasan (audit signing, KMS integration)

Open questions / Risks:
- What level of routing trace detail is safe to export without exposing internal hostnames? (Security to define redaction rules).
- Signatures: use platform KMS -- requires security sign-off and key rotation policy.
- Cost of generating artifacts for long windows could be high; consider rate limits / quotas.

Artifacts & links:
- SLA clause draft: CONFLUENCE: /spaces/COMP/residency-sla-drafts (placeholder)
- Evidence generator prototype repo: github.com/redwood/evidence-gen (prototype branch)
- Design mockups: Drive/Regulatory/HostingProofMockup.png

Notes:
Keep language in manifest intentionally vendor-agnostic and include a short human-readable explanation of any redactions applied.
